report:
The restricted theorem satisfies the original completion criteria. It gives a genuinely divisorial ordinary model reference, a continuous uniformly positive solution residual, singleton supports on all of C(X), a directly defined weak weighted product, and approximation independence for the specified fixed-divisor, uniform-residual-form class. Its singularity, density and positivity restrictions remain essential.

The envelope calculation is valid. Equivariance reduces the envelope to a radial function on the first sphere. Its total potential is convex, and the logarithmic obstacle bounds every slope by a. The tangent construction at r²=a/λ consequently bounds every envelope competitor. The displayed φ attains that bound for C≥C_*: its value and first derivative match at the contact circle, its residual is nonnegative, and 0≤φ−ψ≤C_* off D. Thus Pθ[ψ]=φ, bounded-type invariance gives Pθ[φ]=φ, and sup φ=0. For λ/(a+λ)<ε<1, ψ is an actual εθ-psh candidate below φ, establishing the additional admissibility requirement. The reference has positive finite non-pluripolar mass and an open region of residual degeneracy. Since dd^cθ=(dd^cb)∧ω₂≠0, every smooth positive potential perturbation is non-Gauduchon.

The Green construction also checks out. The chordal logarithmic kernel has dd^c_xG=δ_z−ω₁, zero mean, and absolute integral 2/e. Uniform logarithmic integrability gives a bounded continuous mean-zero w with dd^cw=(A−a)ω₁. Consequently u=ψ+w is canonical, θ-psh, and of the verified model’s bounded singularity type. Off D, adding a sufficiently large strictly psh quadratic permits the Bedford–Taylor recursion. Uniform mollification of the potential and its continuous complex Hessian identifies that recursion with the ordinary square. Smooth-background corrections then give Ω and Ω²; their non-pluripolar extensions discard D and introduce no divisor term. The constructed solution therefore has scalar c=a/m by the task-granted scalar uniqueness.

The weight is defined independently of supports. Multiplication by the smooth positive function ρ=1/(2ab) is legitimate, and Q=[A/(2ab)]ω₁+[1/(2a)]ω₂ is distributionally closed: its first coefficient depends only on the already top-degree first factor. Normalization gives ∫ρΩ²=1. Both signed smooth potential variations remain positive for sufficiently small parameter, and their exact quadratic Monge–Ampère expansion gives D_uMA(h)=2Ω∧dd^ch and L_uh=Δ₁h/A+Δ₂h/b. Distributional integration by parts proves the stated adjoint identity.

Every full supporting probability annihilates this operator. The constructed variation density F_t is continuous even outside the factorized density family, and scalar uniqueness gives Bφ(F_t)=Bφ(F). The support inequality for positive and negative t, together with the uniform expansion F_t−F=tL_uh+O(t²), forces ∫L_uh dμ=0. Thus this step uses the full supporting set, not a restriction to special densities.

The invariant-measure proof is valid for arbitrary Borel probabilities. Spherical-harmonic testing produces finite signed measures T_k satisfying ∫(Δf−λ_k(A/b)f)dT_k=0. The zero mode is a constant multiple of ω₁, fixed to 1/a by normalization. For every nonzero mode, V=λ_kA/b has strictly positive minimum. The heat-resolvent contraction constructs a continuous solution for every continuous right-hand side; heat smoothing approximates both the solution and its Laplacian uniformly. Testing those smooth approximants proves T_k=0 without assuming a density. Polynomial decomposition into spherical harmonics and uniform density of product tests then identify μ=(A/a)dW. Task-granted nonemptiness establishes Aφ(F)={ν}. The same argument proves uniqueness, almost everywhere, of the normalized nonnegative integrable weight because uniform positivity justifies its multiplication by Ω.

Approximation independence includes the actual weighted currents. Uniform positive residual bounds give L_jh→L_uh uniformly, so every weak limit of the normalized classical adjoint probabilities is ν. For each smooth test form ξ, the continuous ratios (Ω_j∧ξ)/Ω_j² converge uniformly. Integrating these ratios against the adjoint probabilities proves ρ_jΩ_j→Q as currents. The corresponding determinant ratios prove ρ_jdW→ρdW as measures. This argument needs no pointwise multiplier bounds. Heat smoothing A supplies admissible smooth approximations and uniform convergence of their Green potentials; adding vanishing smooth nonsymmetric perturbations also preserves admissibility.

The nonsmooth example’s displayed identities verify directly: mean A=1, Monge–Ampère mass 4, and height moments 0 and 5/24. The raw pole smoothing is a valid separate obstruction: D_δ has mass one and concentrates at the divisor, and the explicitly normalized adjoints converge to a probability assigning λ/(1+λ)=1/5 to D. This is incompatible with the task-granted absolute continuity of supports. These approximations lie outside the theorem’s approximation class.

Both external premises were independently checked at their primary sources. Bedford–Taylor equation (2.1), Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2 and the induction proof provide precisely the local recursion and algebraic properties used here. [Bedford–Taylor](https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/117/6320-11511_2006_Article_BF02392348.pdf) Gauduchon’s Section 3, Theorem 2 and its proof establish smooth conformal existence and uniqueness through the one-dimensional adjoint kernel and positivity argument; the even-Betti restriction belongs to Theorem 1 and is irrelevant here. [Gauduchon](https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf) Neither source is being used to supply singular solvability or rough-weight multiplication.

Harmless terminology clarification: “full-type” should read “ordinary-type,” meaning u_j∼φ; no equality of Monge–Ampère mass with the model is established or needed. No substantive repair is required. The result does not cover degenerate solution residuals, arbitrary target densities, arbitrary unbounded potentials, or potential-only convergence. Retained-artifact and execution-history assertions were not used as proof. Unindexed task passages below record granted assumptions and are excluded from the external premises list.

passages.statement: For locally bounded plurisubharmonic potentials on an open subset of C², Bedford–Taylor products are positive currents defined recursively by dd^c(vT) when T is the preceding closed product. They are symmetric and multilinear and agree with ordinary products for smooth potentials.
passages.quote: Thus, the definition is justified as an extension of the operator on smooth functions

passages.statement: On a connected compact complex surface, every smooth strictly positive real (1,1)-form Ω admits a smooth function ρ>0 satisfying dd^c(ρΩ)=0, unique up to multiplication by a positive constant.
passages.quote: Toute métrique hermitienne sur une variété presque complexe compacte de dimension 2m est conforme à une métrique hermitienne standard, unique à homothétie près.
